description: Make the existing renderer full-width and responsive IN THE BROWSER (dropping the Electron quarter-screen constraint) and ensure sign-in is reachable, without changing Electron behavior. All changes are browser-scoped: a web-mode class set only when window.electronAPI is absent, and a new css/web.css scoped under html.web-mode. Covers requirements 1 (keep visual style), 2 (responsive mobile+laptop), 3 (full-width web, no quarter-screen), and 4 (sign-in works in browser). This feature leaves the Electron narrow-column layout untouched.
steps: In index.html <head>, BEFORE the stylesheet <link> tags, add a tiny inline <script> that runs: if (!window.electronAPI) { document.documentElement.classList.add('web-mode'); } - inline and early so the class is set before CSS paints (no flash of the narrow layout). Preserve existing head contents and comment style.
In index.html <head>, after the existing css/*.css links, add <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/web.css"> as the LAST stylesheet so its scoped rules win by source order (no !important).

Create css/web.css. Start with a header comment explaining it is browser-only, scoped under html.web-mode, and never affects Electron. Reuse design tokens from css/style.css (do not invent colors/fonts).

In css/web.css under html.web-mode: drop the quarter-screen constraint by widening the app. Center .page with max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto; and give it comfortable padding; align the nav (#main-nav / .nav) to a matching centered max-width band. Confirm #page-calendar stays full-width (css/calendar.css already sets width:100%; do not shrink it).

In css/web.css under html.web-mode at min-width:1025px: relayout .timer-layout and .timeblock-layout as responsive multi-column grids (e.g. two columns) so wide space is used sensibly; keep single-column below 1025px.

In css/web.css under html.web-mode add @media (max-width:600px) rules making every surface usable on a ~375px phone: nav wraps/stacks and stays tappable; timer controls wrap; scheduler input groups stack full-width; the calendar grid remains usable (allow horizontal scroll if needed); history heatmap scales; and ALL modals fit a 375px viewport with sensible max-width/padding - cover .cw-modal-content (calendar + auth share .cw-modal), .reflection-content, .timeline-content, timer settings/modals, and .auth-modal/.auth-content.

Verify sign-in in the browser: the nav #nav-account 'Sign in' button must open the auth modal (code is already client-side in js/auth/auth-ui.js). Do NOT change auth logic or supabase-config.js credentials.

Audit for Electron-only controls that would render as dead/broken buttons when window.electronAPI is undefined. The renderer already hides #system-windows-section and #startup-setting-row by default - verify, do not rewrite. If any other Electron-only control is visible in the browser (e.g. the minimize-to-overlay button #btn-minimize), hide it via an html.web-mode rule in css/web.css. Make a guarded JS change ONLY if a dead control cannot be handled with CSS.
acceptance_criteria: Serving the repo (python -m http.server 8080) and opening http://localhost:8080/index.html shows <html> with class 'web-mode' and css/web.css loading with status 200 in DevTools.

At 1440px the app content is a centered wide column (max-width ~1200px), NOT the ~360px quarter-width; the nav aligns with it; the Calendar page fills the width; Timer and Scheduler use a multi-column layout.
At 375px every page (Timer, Scheduler, Calendar, History, Read) is usable with no horizontal overflow, and the auth modal, reflection modal, and a calendar event editor each fit within the viewport.
Clicking the nav 'Sign in' button opens the auth modal; navigating all pages produces NO uncaught console errors from missing electronAPI.
Removing the 'web-mode' class in DevTools returns the layout to the narrow Electron look (proving changes are browser-scoped), and `npm test` still reports 61 passing / 0 failing.
verification: Run `npm test` from the repo root and confirm 61 tests pass, 0 fail (no auth/logic regression).

Run `python -m http.server 8080` from the repo root, open http://localhost:8080/index.html, and in DevTools confirm: html.web-mode is present, css/web.css is 200, and the console is clean while clicking through Timer/Scheduler/Calendar/History/Read.
Use DevTools responsive mode at 375px and 1440px to confirm the layout criteria above (full-width centered at desktop, single-column no-overflow at mobile, modals fit).
Click #nav-account and confirm the auth modal opens.
Toggle the 'web-mode' class off on <html> in DevTools and confirm the narrow Electron layout returns (web changes are fully scoped).
findings: WEB-MODE MECHANISM: index.html <head> now has (1) an inline <script> immediately after <title> (before any stylesheet <link>) that runs `if (!window.electronAPI) { document.documentElement.classList.add('web-mode'); }` - this is the single source of the web-mode toggle; (2) `<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/web.css">` as the LAST stylesheet (after css/auth.css). All browser-only rules live in the NEW css/web.css, every selector scoped under `html.web-mode`, no !important. For FEAT-002 (marketing site under web/): the app shell is reachable at /index.html; reuse the same detection pattern if you need web-only behavior, and reuse css/style.css design tokens (--primary #4361ee, --bg #f8f9fa, --surface #fff, --text #1a1a2e, --accent #f72585, --border #e9ecef, --radius 10px, --font 'Segoe UI'...). SIGN-IN DEEP-LINK: there is NO query-param/hash deep-link hook yet. Sign-in is opened only by clicking nav #nav-account (wired in js/auth/auth-ui.js -> openModal). auth-ui.js ALSO exposes `window.openAuthModal` globally, so a marketing 'Sign in' link that lands on /index.html can trigger the modal by calling window.openAuthModal() (e.g. via a small inline script that checks for a ?signin or #signin flag). The auth modal is built dynamically (class 'cw-modal auth-modal' appended to <body>); it reuses .cw-modal/.cw-modal-content from calendar.css plus .auth-content from auth.css. supabase-config.js isConfigured()===true so the real email-OTP flow runs; persistSession:false means browser sign-in is per-session (no cross-reload persistence) - acceptable and unchanged. ELECTRON-ONLY CONTROLS: audited, no CSS/JS hiding was needed. #btn-minimize starts style=display:none and is only shown via `if (isElectron)` in js/timer.js; #system-windows-section and #startup-setting-row likewise start hidden and are only revealed inside `if (isElectron)`/electronAPI guards. So no dead buttons render in the browser and I added no web-mode hide rules for them. The #page-online tab stays visible but its [data-requires-auth] body is gated by js/auth/gate.js (lock overlay when signed out) - unchanged. RESPONSIVE: desktop >=1025px gives .timer-layout a 2-col grid and .timeblock-layout a 3-col grid; tablet 601-1024px gives .timeblock-layout a 2-col grid; mobile <=600px stacks nav/inputs, wraps timer controls, allows horizontal scroll on the calendar grids, and shrinks all modals to max-width:100%/padding:1rem. #page-calendar is explicitly kept full-width (max-width:none). VERIFIED: `npm test` = 61 pass / 0 fail; static server (python -m http.server 8080) serves /index.html 200 and /css/web.css 200; inline web-mode script present and web.css confirmed as the last stylesheet link.
